Paper_Metadata.Paper_Title: Tailoring thickness debit for high-temperature fatigue resistance of Inconel 718 superalloy fabricated by laser powder bed fusion

Composition_Info.Note: The paper states that the chemical composition of the argon-atomized Inconel 718 powder was reported in a previous work and does not reproduce the numerical composition in the current article.

Process_Info.Process_Category: LPBF + stress relief + homogenization + two-step aging + grinding/electropolishing

Process_Text.original: Argon-atomized Inconel 718 powder with a median diameter of D50 = 24.10 μm was used as raw material in the LPBF fabrication. An LPBF machine (EOSINT M270D, EOS, Germany) equipped with a Yb fiber laser source was selected to fabricate an Inconel 718 block with dimensions of 60 mm × 45 mm × 45 mm. The processing parameters including the laser power, scanning speed, hatch spacing, layer thickness, and rotation angle between the successive layers were selected as 285 W, 960 mm/s, 0.100 mm, 0.040 mm, and 67°, respectively. After the LPBF fabrication, the block was heated at 600 °C for 2 h and then cooled in the furnace for stress relief. All the thin-walled specimens with different thicknesses were wire-electrical-discharge cut from the as-fabricated block at the same height and grouped according to the thickness. Two groups of specimens designated HA1065 and HA1100 were homogenized at 1065 °C and 1100 °C for 1 h, respectively, and then subjected to a two-step aging of 760 °C - 10 h/furnace cooling to 650 °C at 55 °C/h + 650 °C - 8 h/air cooling to RT. After the heat treatment, the tensile specimens with gauge dimensions of 6 mm × 1.5 mm × 1.1 mm were ground and electropolished to the thickness of 0.75 mm, and each group of the fatigue specimens to the thicknesses of 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, and 2.00 mm, respectively, with a tolerance of ± 0.05 mm. The front surface (X-Z plane) and the side surfaces (Y-Z plane) of each specimen were mechanically grounded and electropolished to minimize the effect of surface conditions.
Process_Text.simplified: Inconel 718 powder with D50 of 24.10 μm was processed by LPBF on an EOSINT M270D using 285 W laser power, 960 mm/s scan speed, 0.100 mm hatch spacing, 0.040 mm layer thickness, and 67° rotation between successive layers to build a 60 mm × 45 mm × 45 mm block. The block was stress relieved at 600 °C for 2 h with furnace cooling. Thin-walled specimens were wire-EDM cut from the same height of the block. The HA1065 group was homogenized at 1065 °C for 1 h and then two-step aged at 760 °C for 10 h, furnace cooled to 650 °C at 55 °C/h, and held at 650 °C for 8 h followed by air cooling to room temperature. Tensile specimens were finished to 0.75 mm thickness, and fatigue specimens were finished to 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, and 2.00 mm with ±0.05 mm tolerance. Front and side surfaces were ground and electropolished.

Process_Info.Equipment: EOSINT M270D (EOS, Germany) with Yb fiber laser source

Key_Params.Cooling_Medium: furnace cooling to 650 °C at 55 °C/h, then air cooling to room temperature

Microstructure_Text.original: A typical 3D-XRT image of the pores in the cylindrical specimen indicates that many spherical pores are uniformly distributed. All the pores have a sphericity greater than 0.8, indicating the pores in the XRT specimen are near-spherical gas pores. In addition, there are 95 % of the pores have an equivalent diameter of < 24 μm. According to the volume of all the pores and the XRT specimen, the porosity is 0.01 % and the calculation density of the specimen is 99.99 %. The HA1065 specimen consists of epitaxial columnar and V-shaped grains. Approximately 94 % of grains were divided into four types, <001>, <101>, <111> and <112>, color-coded based on the misorientation between the BD and the grain orientation. A small number of columnar grains with <001>//BD and a large amount of V-shaped grains with <101>//BD are distributed alternately. The area-weighted grain diameter was calculated as dHA1065 = 58.5 μm using Y-Z plane EBSD maps. SEM observations show many elongated Laves phases along the dendritic boundaries or irregular particle-like Laves phases at the grain boundaries, and many rod-like or needle-like δ phases distributed at the grain boundaries. The precipitates distributed along the grain boundaries in the HA1065 specimen are much more than those in the HA1100 one. The spacing between adjacent precipitates at grain boundaries in the HA1065 specimen is much smaller than that in the HA1100 specimen. The precipitates in the HA1065 specimen are longer but narrower than those in the HA1100 one, and their aspect ratio is larger. TEM bright field images show few spherical γ′ phases and lots of ellipsoidal γ″ phases. The average spacing of γ″ phases in the HA1065 specimen is close to that in the HA1100 specimen, while the average length of γ″ phases in the former is shorter than that in the latter. Fatigue cracks of all the specimens mainly initiated from the surface. When t = 0.25 mm, there is a typical feature of quasi-cleavage fracture, and cracks are initiated from the microstructural defects near the surface with cleavage steps or river-like patterns. When t = 2.00 mm, the crack initiation zones are relatively flat and exhibit river-like patterns. In the propagation zones, fatigue striations were formed when cracks propagated through grains. The intergranular fracture regions exhibit a rough surface of dendrite boundaries and precipitates for the HA1065 specimen.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: HA1065 inherits the low-porosity LPBF pore population of near-spherical gas pores and contains epitaxial columnar plus V-shaped grains with a strong morphology-related texture. Its area-weighted grain diameter is 58.5 μm. Grain boundaries contain abundant elongated Laves, irregular Laves, and rod-like or needle-like δ phases with relatively small spacing and high aspect ratio. The matrix also contains γ′ and γ″ precipitates, with γ″ being the dominant strengthening precipitate considered by the authors. Under fatigue at 650 °C, cracks mainly initiate from the surface. The thinnest specimens show quasi-cleavage features and surface-near microstructural crack initiation, whereas thicker specimens show flatter initiation zones and mixed intergranular-transgranular propagation.

Microstructure_Text.original: A typical 3D-XRT image of the pores in the cylindrical specimen indicates that many spherical pores are uniformly distributed. All the pores have a sphericity greater than 0.8, indicating the pores in the XRT specimen are near-spherical gas pores. In addition, there are 95 % of the pores have an equivalent diameter of < 24 μm. According to the volume of all the pores and the XRT specimen, the porosity is 0.01 % and the calculation density of the specimen is 99.99 %. The HA1100 specimen only has relatively equiaxed grains due to the recrystallization and grain growth. There are lots of annealing twins in the HA1100 specimen. The area-weighted grain diameter was calculated as dHA1100 = 54.1 μm using Y-Z plane EBSD maps. SEM observations show many particle-like carbides distributing at the grain boundaries. The precipitates distributed along the grain boundaries in the HA1100 specimen are much fewer than those in the HA1065 specimen. The spacing between adjacent precipitates at grain boundaries in the HA1100 specimen is much larger than that in the HA1065 specimen. The precipitates in the HA1100 specimen are less elongated and have a lower aspect ratio than those in the HA1065 specimen. TEM bright field images show few spherical γ′ phases and lots of ellipsoidal γ″ phases. The average spacing of γ″ phases in the HA1100 specimen is close to that in the HA1065 specimen, while the average length of γ″ phases in the HA1100 specimen is longer and the volume fraction is higher. Fatigue cracks of all the specimens mainly initiated from the surface. When t = 0.25 mm, there is a typical feature of quasi-cleavage fracture, and cracks are initiated from the microstructural defects near the surface with cleavage steps or river-like patterns. When t = 2.00 mm, the crack initiation zones are relatively flat and exhibit river-like patterns. In the propagation zones, fatigue striations were formed when cracks propagated through grains. The intergranular fracture regions exhibit smooth grain-boundary surfaces for the HA1100 specimen.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: HA1100 inherits the low-porosity LPBF pore population of near-spherical gas pores and contains relatively equiaxed recrystallized grains with many annealing twins. Its area-weighted grain diameter is 54.1 μm. Grain boundaries mainly contain particle-like carbides, and harmful elongated Laves and dense grain-boundary precipitates are much less prevalent than in HA1065. The matrix contains γ′ and γ″ precipitates, with HA1100 showing longer and more abundant γ″. Under fatigue at 650 °C, cracks mainly initiate from the surface. The thinnest specimens show quasi-cleavage initiation from surface-near microstructural defects, whereas thicker specimens show flatter initiation zones and mixed intergranular-transgranular propagation with smoother intergranular surfaces than HA1065.
